profiles.meeting_scenario: A troubleshooting meeting at a research-oriented solver team maintaining an answer set solver and its automated fuzzing pipeline. Overnight fuzzing on the `stable-core` branch produced several minimized ASP programs that trigger a mismatch between the in-house solver `OrchidASP` and a trusted cross-check harness, and one case also causes a timeout regression after delta debugging. The immediate agenda is to diagnose whether the failures point to a real solver bug, a harness/minimizer artifact, or an expected difference caused by configuration drift, and to decide what short-term fix to apply before the next benchmark run. The expected outcome is agreement on the suspected root cause and a concrete action plan for reproducing, validating, and patching the issue.

members.name: Nina Kovacs
members.expertise: CDNL-based answer set solving, grounding/solving interfaces, regression triage
members.background: Nina has spent four years developing the solver core of OrchidASP, especially unsat-core optimization and model verification paths, and she usually debugs from minimized reproducers produced by the fuzzing farm.
members.private_state: She wants to keep the issue scoped to a solver-side reproducible defect in the current `stable-core` branch so she can patch it quickly before the upcoming artifact freeze; she is worried that if the problem turns out to involve the harness or environment, the timeline will expand beyond her control.
hidden_assumptions: When someone says a case 'fails on stable-core', they mean the current local branch head built with the team's standard release-like flags and default verification enabled.
A 'reduced reproducer' should preserve the semantic bug class, even if the exact runtime profile changes during shrinking.
If a bug is described as 'fixed', that means the minimized program no longer yields an invalid answer set or missed model on the standard single-shot solver path.
When discussing the 'same seed' from fuzzing, the relevant object is the final minimized `.lp` file attached to the ticket rather than the original generated program or the random generator state.

members.name: Leo Marin
members.expertise: Grammar-based fuzzing, delta debugging, solver comparison harnesses, CI reproducibility
members.background: Leo built most of the team's black-box ASP fuzzing and shrinking pipeline, including the cross-solver oracle checks and containerized CI runners that execute nightly campaigns.
members.private_state: He wants to confirm that the nightly failure is stable enough to justify changes to the minimizer or harness settings, because repeated false alarms from configuration mismatches would undermine confidence in his tooling; he is also concerned about preserving the exact CI conditions that exposed the issue.
hidden_assumptions: When someone says a case 'fails on stable-core', they mean the nightly CI container image and the exact build artifact produced there, including compile-time feature toggles.
A 'reduced reproducer' is acceptable only if it still reproduces under the same oracle comparison and timeout conditions as the original failing CI job.
If a bug is 'fixed', that means the nightly pipeline no longer flags the case across the full differential harness, including optimization mode and timeout checks.
When discussing the 'same seed' from fuzzing, the relevant object is the generator seed and grammar configuration that can regenerate the original failing family of programs.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They both refer to reproducing the issue on 'stable-core' or 'the stable build'.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means her local checkout at the current `stable-core` HEAD, compiled with the standard release profile and runtime model verification enabled.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the nightly CI container artifact from `stable-core`, compiled with the harness image's feature flags, including verification-off and a different allocator.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both assume the branch name is a sufficiently precise reference, and in a mature engineering team 'stable-core' sounds like a single obvious thing rather than a family of slightly different artifacts.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as the reduced reproducer
misalignment_points.surface_form: They both talk about 'the reduced case' and whether it still reproduces.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the minimized `.lp` file attached to the bug ticket, as long as it still demonstrates the same semantic defect class in OrchidASP.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the delta-debugged case together with the harness invocation conditions, where reproduction includes preserving the differential mismatch or timeout observed in CI.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In debugging culture, 'reduced case' is a routine phrase, and both are used to treating the reduction artifact as self-explanatory, even though one centers the input file and the other centers the full experimental setup.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They both discuss shipping a 'fix' before the next benchmark run.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 thinks the issue is fixed if OrchidASP stops producing an invalid answer set or missing a model on the minimized single-shot case, even if runtime remains worse than before and the broader campaign is not rerun yet.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 thinks the issue is fixed only if the nightly fuzzing pipeline stops flagging the seed family under the differential oracle, including the timeout regression that appeared after shrinking.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both are cooperating toward resolution and use the same success language, but each imports their usual local quality bar: solver-core correctness for M1 and pipeline-level non-regression for M2.

misalignment_points.topic: What to 'rerun with the same seed' entails
misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree to rerun the issue 'with the same seed' to validate the diagnosis.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 plans to rerun the attached minimized program directly through the solver with a deterministic command line, treating the random seed as irrelevant once the file exists.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 plans to rerun the grammar fuzzer and shrinker using the original generator seed, grammar version, and harness configuration to see whether the same failing family reappears.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Seed-based workflows are common in fuzzing, so 'same seed' sounds precise; however, Nina informally uses it as shorthand for the ticketed reproducer, while Leo uses it literally as a generation procedure.
